payload.field_feedback: Six pieces came back from the field since the last ship, all from the owner using the system live. (1) THE SHIP DID NOT COMMIT - i8c completed its process and merged nothing, because the close-and-merge split was never built; 45 files sat uncommitted on trunk. (2) The tools were not worktree-aware - an iteration running in its worktree had its files land on trunk. (3) The QR opened the browser, not the app - twice wrong before matching v1's ntfy:// deep link, a porting regression from v1's ask.go. (4) Commit rhythm corrected: commit at MILESTONES onto the iteration's branch; trunk receives everything only when the iteration is done. (5) One-click install is the goal, not zero-dep - declare a dependency if it keeps install one-click, and if you vendor, credit loudly. (6) Do not render the live board back at the owner while they are looking at it.

payload.call_log_mined: 3,304 calls, 137 not-ok (4.1%). Clause distribution: SE-C-046 missing update on submit (7), SE-C-064 patch old_string not uniquely found (5), SE-C-030 (6), SE-C-005 unadmitted after a reconnect (4), SE-C-040 toll (3), SE-C-061 file not found (3), SE-C-065 ledger path through the wrong lane (2), SE-C-053 battery scope (2), SE-C-063 CAS hash (1), SE-C-047 commit window (1); 99 carry no clause (mostly non-zero exits from deliberate red runs, not rejections). Lane shape: se_file_patch 566 vs se_file_write 127 - patching is the dominant write mode by 4.5x. se_help was called 31 times; hits and misses are not separable in the current record, which is itself a gap since the miss IS the missing-tool demand signal. Leads drawn: the patch/write ratio and the SE-C-064 failures point at the same hazard (below); the SE-C-005 cluster is the reconnect resetting admission mid-run. Self-witness: this very submit was rejected by SE-C-046, the clause already at the top of the list - the update rides every submit, and the rule is still being learned by habit rather than enforced at the point of composition.
payload.waste_leads: Two real wastes, both of which this iteration removes or names. (1) MANUAL SYNCING BETWEEN WORKTREE AND TRUNK - because nothing commits to the branch and the merge does not work, i8c's content had to be hand-copied between the two roots repeatedly, and one file (i8c's four acceptance tests) ended up existing ONLY in the worktree, where removing that directory would have destroyed it. That is precisely the waste the close-and-merge split exists to abolish. (2) PATCHING ENGINE SOURCES leaves broken intermediate states: an incremental patch series on tools.ts left the file referencing a symbol that did not exist yet, and the running engine hot-reloaded that broken state mid-edit, which cost a full whole-file rewrite to recover. The repo already carries the rule (prefer one whole-file write when you hold the whole file); the 4.5:1 patch-to-write ratio says it is not being followed for engine sources.
payload.process_stale: The METHOD is not stale, but it is under-implemented against its own design, and that is this iteration's whole point. se-v2-design §4 has specified the close-and-merge split since the design was written - main holds live claims, branches hold the record of how they got there, the merge tree carries only live claims, the tag is mandatory - and none of it was ever built. The gap only became visible when a real iteration shipped and produced no commit. Standing lesson for the state-of-the-art check: a design section that no test touches is indistinguishable from a design section that was never written, so the check should compare the design document against the engine, not only the process against the outside world.
